content.title: Does an Unexpected Guest in Hard Times Make You Anxious?
content.subtitle: A moving story of a couple who hid their hunger in the dark to honor their guest!
content.body:
The somber shadows of evening were falling over the air of Madinah. All around hung the silent, unbearable ache of hunger and poverty. At such a moment, a weary and starving man came to stand before the Prophet ﷺ. With a broken voice, he pleaded, "O Messenger of Allah! I am severely hungry and in distress."

The Prophet ﷺ immediately sent word to the homes of all his wives—asking if there was even a little food for the guest. Yet, the exact same reply returned from every single household—"By Him Who sent you with the truth! I have nothing in my house except water." With a heavy heart, the Prophet ﷺ looked at his companions and asked, "Who will host and feed this guest tonight? May Allah have mercy on him!"

The Silent Sacrifice of an Ansar Couple

From the crowd of companions, Abu Talha Al-Ansari (RA) stepped forward. He said, "O Messenger of Allah! I will take him." Taking the guest home, he quietly asked his wife, Umm Sulaym (RA), "Do you have any food?" His wife calmly replied, "No, there is only a small portion meant for my children's dinner."

To them, honoring the Prophet's guest meant far more than their own children's hunger. Abu Talha (RA) said, "Distract the children somehow and put them to sleep. And when the guest sits down to eat, get up on the pretext of fixing the lamp and turn it off!" Umm Sulaym (RA) hugged her hungry children close and put them to sleep unfed. As soon as the guest sat down to eat, she extinguished the lamp. In the pitch darkness, the guest ate to his heart's content, while Abu Talha (RA) and his wife merely moved their hands over empty plates—so the guest would not feel embarrassed!

A Sacrifice That Made Allah Smile

That night, the husband, wife, and children endured the hours completely unfed. Yet, their extraordinary sacrifice deeply pleased the Lord of the Throne. The next morning, as soon as Abu Talha (RA) arrived at the Prophet's ﷺ gathering, the Prophet ﷺ smiled gently upon seeing him and said, "Allah Ta'ala was pleased and smiled at the way you both treated your guest last night!"

Following this event, Allah revealed that eternal verse in the Quran:

"And they give preference to others over themselves, even though they themselves are in need. And whoever is saved from the selfishness of their own souls, it is they who are truly successful."

What Is Our Reality in Hard Times?

Let us pause and look at ourselves! Today, when our households face slight financial strain or our pockets run empty toward the end of the month, a guest's arrival becomes a source of extreme annoyance. Especially the mothers and sisters at home get deeply irritated under the pressure of chores and scarcity, sighing quietly in a corner of the kitchen. We think, we are barely managing ourselves; how will we handle a guest now! We view guests as a burden, and even breathe a sigh of relief when they leave. Yet, the Prophet ﷺ warned: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honor his guest."

Let Scarcity Be the Key to Barakah

Never forget, a guest never comes to take a share of your sustenance; rather, they knock on your door, bringing their own provision and blessings into your home. As mentioned in the Hadith: "The food of one person is sufficient for two, and the food of two is sufficient for four."

During hard times, whatever humble lentils and rice you have at home, serve it to your guest with a smile and zero irritation. Like Umm Sulaym (RA), your modest sacrifice and sincerity might just please the Lord of the Throne, and through that, Allah may open unimaginable doors of sustenance and Barakah in your struggling household!

References:

  1. Incident of Abu Talha (RA): Sahih Bukhari (Hadith 3798, 4889) & Sahih Muslim (Hadith 2054)

  2. Verse on selflessness: Al-Quran, Surah Al-Hashr (Verse 9)

  3. Command to honor guests: Sahih Bukhari (Hadith 6018, 6136) & Sahih Muslim (Hadith 47)

  4. Hadith on Barakah in food: Sahih Muslim (Hadith 2059) & Sahih Bukhari (Hadith 5392)
